history.summary: PROVISIONAL RECORD: no web source documents any Sai Baba temple in Churachandpur - its location, founding date and management are all unpublished and marked (verify) throughout this record. Searches returned only Sai Baba temples in other states/places (Thane, Agartala, Bishnupur town - the latter marked permanently closed on listings, 17+ km from Churachandpur) and none in Churachandpur town. What is verifiable is the local context: Churachandpur (Lamka) is the Kuki-Chin heartland, overwhelmingly Christian, with a small non-tribal Hindu community (traders, government employees and their families) that maintains a handful of shrines in and around the town - a onefivenine directory lists the Meigeingakpa/Maigheingakpa temples in central Lamka, the Shree Radha Krishna Mandir at Jangnomphai, and a Durga Temple at Saiton, while a 2023 YouTube video documents at least one functioning Hindu temple in the town left untouched during the ethnic violence. A Sai Baba shrine serving this community may exist; nothing about it could be confirmed online. Do not invent a location or founding date - this entry must be verified on the ground before use. town_description: Churachandpur (locally called Lamka) is the second-largest town of Manipur and the headquarters of Churachandpur district, about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road. It is the heartland of the Kuki-Chin hill tribes (Thadou-Kuki, Hmar, Paite, Zou) and is overwhelmingly Christian; a small Hindu/Meitei community maintains a handful of shrines in and around the town. Khuga Dam, about 12 km south, is the district's main reservoir and picnic viewpoint.
